gen-gf-handlee-switzer: Hand-drawn and tightly gathered, Handlee has strokes that vary just enough. Switzer brings a wire-like sans with constant pen pressure, and it works better when the text stays brief.
gen-gf-handlee-work-sans: Work Sans is a plain sans whose curves carry the full weight of its straight stems. And Handlee brings mild, hand-drawn strokes that lend charm, mostly when the text is brief.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-epunda-slab: Happy Monkey does its best work loud, with ruler-straight lines and wide gaps in the e. And Epunda Slab does its best work quietly, in tall rounded lowercase with classic dignity.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-kadwa: Happy Monkey comes in bold, with letterforms like bent tubing and moderate lowercase height. And beside it Kadwa, a classic serif with a larger-than-usual x-height, feels taller and more editorial.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-piazzolla: Piazzolla reads refined and authoritative, its lowercase nearly matching the capitals and its e pried open. But Happy Monkey, with its ruler-straight line, loses its swagger if made small, so let it stand large.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-scope-one: Happy Monkey draws a steady, unshaded outline with wide gaps in the e, bold and distinctive. And Scope One adds refined, traditional weight through stubby ascenders and counters that spill into surrounding space.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-slabo-13px: Round-nibbed and bold, Happy Monkey stands out the moment it appears. Slabo 13px, a bookish serif with large open counters, is happiest at modest sizes, so leave the big type to the heading.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-suwannaphum: Happy Monkey runs parallel stroke edges through every curve, which keeps it bold and distinctive. Suwannaphum, a dignified serif with a high x-height and a wide-open c, reads in a steady editorial voice.
gen-gf-hi-melody-fs-neco: Neco carries an authoritative, dignified voice, its strokes swelling gently from hairline to stem without ever pinching shut. Hi Melody adds huddled, hand-drawn warmth, best kept to brief lines.
gen-gf-hi-melody-fs-plein: Huddled and hand-drawn, Hi Melody feels thoroughly inviting and casual. Plein, a reliable, clean sans-serif with a clear channel into each round letter, is comfortable at a modest size.
